new.title: See Hadrian's Gate, the Roman arch of Antalya
new.desc: A three-arched marble gateway built around 130 CE to honour Emperor Hadrian's visit to the city. It is the only surviving ancient entrance into the old town and still opens onto Kaleiçi.
new.tip: Best photographed in early morning before the crowds; entry is free.

new.title: Look up at the fluted Yivli Minare
new.desc: Built in the early 13th century under Seljuk sultan Alaeddin Keykubad I, the Yivli Minare is the symbol of Antalya. Its eight-grooved brick shaft is decorated with dark blue tiles.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times with covered shoulders and knees; entry is free.
new.q: Yivli Minare Camii, Kaleiçi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Climb to Hıdırlık Tower above the sea
new.desc: A 14 m Roman-era round tower at the south-western corner of the old walls, dated to the 1st-2nd century CE. It stands on a cliff edge with views over the harbour and the Taurus mountains.
new.tip: Go at sunset when the Beydağları peaks turn pink; there is no entry fee.

new.title: Explore the ruined Kesik Minare
new.desc: A Roman temple became a Byzantine church, then a mosque under the Seljuks, and a fire in 1896 left only the stump of the minaret. Brick walls and the apse now stand open to the sky.
new.tip: The ruins are visible from the street; combine with a wander through nearby lanes.

new.title: Meet friends at the Antalya Clock Tower
new.desc: The Saat Kulesi was built in 1901 to mark 25 years of Sultan Abdulhamid II's reign and stands at Kalekapısı, the main gate to Kaleiçi. The square around it is the traditional meeting point of the city.
new.tip: Street musicians play on the square in the evening; the old bazaar starts just north.

new.title: Tour the Antalya Museum and its Perge statues
new.desc: One of Turkey's major archaeology museums, with a hall of Roman marble gods from Perge, rich sarcophagi and finds from Karain Cave. Collections run from the Palaeolithic to the Ottoman period.
new.tip: Allow two hours; the Nostalji tram stops nearby. Usually closed on Mondays.
new.q: Antalya Müzesi, Konyaaltı Caddesi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Watch sunset from the Karaalioğlu Park cliffs
new.desc: A large seaside park on the cliffs west of Kaleiçi with rose gardens, pines, palms and sculptures. Clifftop paths face the Beydağları across the bay.
new.tip: Come an hour before sunset; tea gardens line the edge.

new.title: See the Seljuk Karatay Medresesi
new.desc: A theological school built in 1251 by vizier Celaleddin Karatay, with a carved stone portal. It now serves as a cultural centre and café.
new.tip: A short stroll from the Clock Tower; check opening hours.

new.title: Step into the Ottoman Tekeli Mehmet Paşa Mosque
new.desc: An Ottoman mosque of 1796 near the harbour, built by the local governor Tekeli Mehmet Pasha. It is among the notable monuments of Kaleiçi.
new.tip: Visit between prayers and dress modestly.
new.q: Tekeli Mehmet Paşa Camii, Kaleiçi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Visit the Suna and İnan Kıraç Kaleiçi Museum
new.desc: A restored historic house complex in Kaleiçi showing Kütahya tiles and ceramics and displays of local life. It is run by the Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation.
new.tip: Quiet in the afternoon; check opening days.
new.q: Suna ve İnan Kıraç Kaleiçi Müzesi, Kaleiçi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Walk the colonnaded streets of ancient Perge
new.desc: A leading Pamphylian city with a Roman theatre, stadium, Hellenistic gate towers and a colonnaded street with a central water channel. St Paul preached here around 46 CE.
new.tip: Go at opening time in summer, it is shadeless; about 15 km east of the centre.

new.title: Hike up to the mountain city of Termessos
new.desc: A Pisidian city high on Güllük Dağı that Alexander the Great could not take. Its theatre looks across the Taurus, with rock tombs and a Roman gymnasium among the pines.
new.tip: Plan half a day with water and sturdy shoes; about 35 km northwest, so a car or tour helps.
new.q: Termessos Antik Kenti, Güllük Dağı Milli Parkı, Döşemealtı, Antalya

new.title: Stand behind the Upper Düden Waterfalls
new.desc: Düden stream drops about 20 m in a park in Kepez, about 9 km north of the centre, and a path leads behind the curtain of water.
new.tip: Take bus VN66 or a taxi; the path behind the falls is slippery.

new.title: See the Lower Düden Falls plunge into the sea
new.desc: Aşağı Düden drops about 40 m over a cliff directly into the Mediterranean in a park by the Lara road, with a path to a viewpoint above the spray.
new.tip: Also visible from boats leaving the old harbour; small entry fee.
new.q: Aşağı Düden Şelalesi, Lara Caddesi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Picnic at Kurşunlu Waterfall Nature Park
new.desc: A waterfall of about 18 m among pines near Aksu, in a 33-hectare nature park about 20 km northeast of the city.
new.tip: Mornings are calmer; combine with Perge nearby.
new.q: Kurşunlu Şelalesi Tabiat Parkı, Aksu, Antalya

new.title: Ride the Tünektepe cable car for bay views
new.desc: A cable car climbs the 618 m Tünek Tepe from the Sarısu coast to a lookout with café and restaurant above Konyaaltı and the Taurus mountains.
new.tip: Check that the cable car is running; go for sunset.

new.title: Swim at Konyaaltı Beach beneath the Taurus peaks
new.desc: A Blue Flag pebble beach about 13 km long running west of the city with the Beydağları rising behind it, a promenade and cafés along the front.
new.tip: Wear water shoes for the pebbles.

new.title: Lie on the sand at Lara Beach
new.desc: A long sandy beach east of the centre, sandier than Konyaaltı, with beach clubs and the public Lara Halk Plajı.
new.tip: Shallow water suits families; take a bus from the centre.
new.q: Lara Halk Plajı, Lara, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Swim at tiny Mermerli Beach under the city walls
new.desc: A small pebble beach backed by the ancient sea walls beside the harbour, reached by stairs through the Mermerli restaurant.
new.tip: Pay the small beach fee at the stairs and stay for the sunset.
new.q: Mermerli Plajı, Mermerli Sokak, Kaleiçi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Take a boat trip from the Old Harbour past the cliffs
new.desc: Boats leave the historic Kaleiçi harbour for coastal cruises along the limestone cliffs, past the Lower Düden Falls and the Lara coast.
new.tip: Compare prices at the jetty; morning trips are calmer.
new.q: Kaleiçi Yat Limanı, Kaleiçi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Steam in a traditional hammam in Kaleiçi
new.desc: Sefa Hamamı offers an Ottoman-style bath with a hot marble stone, scrub and foam massage in the old town.
new.tip: Book ahead in summer.

new.title: Scrub up at Demirhan Hamamı, a local favourite
new.desc: A neighbourhood hammam near Kaleiçi popular with Antalya residents rather than tour groups, with scrub and massage.
new.tip: Go in the early evening; check men's and women's sessions.
new.q: Demirhan Hamamı, Kışla 34. Sokak No:4, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Walk the tunnel at Antalya Aquarium
new.desc: One of Europe's larger aquariums, with a long glass tunnel and a snow world near the Konyaaltı shore.
new.tip: Quiet on weekday mornings; booking online is cheaper.

new.title: Ride the Nostalgic Tram along the coast
new.desc: A heritage line about 4.7 km long, opened in 1999 with former Nuremberg trams, runs from the edge of Kaleiçi along the cliff front to the Antalya Museum.
new.tip: Board near Karaalioğlu Park.

new.title: Browse the Old Bazaar for spices and leather
new.desc: Narrow streets north of the Clock Tower hold souvenirs, spices, carpets, jewellery and food stalls in the traditional market quarter.
new.tip: Bargain politely; busiest in the evening.

new.title: See the giant sand sculptures at Sandland
new.desc: A seasonal open-air show of huge sand sculptures on the Lara coast road, with a new theme each year.
new.tip: Check season and opening times first.

new.title: Order the piyaz at Özgül Kebap
new.desc: A small lunch spot in Elmalı known for Antalya's tahini piyaz, a white-bean salad, plus good şiş köfte.
new.tip: Go for lunch; piyaz with şiş köfte is the classic order.

new.title: Eat şiş köfte and piyaz at Arap Nazmi
new.desc: A piyaz and şiş köfte restaurant serving the local pairing of grilled minced-meat skewers with tahini bean salad.
new.tip: Try the burger made with şiş köfte meat.

new.title: Grill lamb and köfte at Şişçi Ramazan
new.desc: A skewer house known for köfte, lamb and chicken cooked over coals, and for Antalya-style tahini piyaz.
new.tip: Order mixed şiş with piyaz and ayran.

new.title: Taste kuzu tandır at Antalya Balık Evi
new.desc: A seafood restaurant with Mediterranean views, also praised for slow-cooked lamb tandır.
new.tip: Reserve a terrace table at sunset.
new.q: Antalya Balık Evi, Çağlayan Mahallesi, 2057 Sokak No:2, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Eat kebab at Kadirşinas Ocakbaşı
new.desc: A fireside ocakbaşı grill serving kebabs, listed by National Geographic among Antalya's eateries for locals.
new.tip: Sit at the counter around the grill.

new.title: Share meze at Kaleiçi Meyhane
new.desc: A meyhane in the heart of the old town with a long meze list, hot starters and fresh seafood.
new.tip: Order raki with a set of meze; reserve for weekends.

new.title: Grill sea bass at Lara Balık
new.desc: A shore-side seafood restaurant with terrace views, known for grilled sea bass, calamari and prawns.
new.tip: Book a sea-facing table at dusk.
new.q: Lara Balık, Tevfik Işık Caddesi 8, Lara, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Dine on the marina at Arma Restaurant
new.desc: An upscale seafood restaurant with marina views in Muratpaşa.
new.tip: Reserve a terrace table at sunset.
new.q: Arma Restaurant, Kaleiçi Yat Limanı, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Eat grilled meat at 7 Mehmet above the bay
new.desc: A family restaurant that began as a soup shop in 1937, now on a hill terrace over Konyaaltı with grilled meats, seafood and meze.
new.tip: Arrive before sunset for the views.
new.q: 7 Mehmet Restaurant, Konyaaltı Caddesi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Dine at Seraser in a 300-year-old house
new.desc: A fine-dining restaurant in a historic Kaleiçi house on Mermerli Sokak, with an Ottoman-influenced menu and a Turkish breakfast.
new.tip: Reserve the courtyard; expensive.
new.q: Seraser Fine Dining Restaurant, Mermerli Sokak, Kaleiçi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Eat roast chicken at Parlak Restaurant
new.desc: An informal grill famous for whole roasted chicken served with rice or bulgur.
new.tip: Share a whole bird; budget friendly.
new.q: Parlak Restaurant, Kazım Özalp Caddesi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Hear folk music at Hasan Ağa
new.desc: A restaurant combining Turkish meat dishes with live folk music.
new.tip: Go in the evening for the music.
new.q: Hasanağa Restaurant, Mescit Sokak 15, Kaleiçi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Eat Antalya tahini piyaz at Piyazcı Ahmet
new.desc: Piyazcı Ahmet has served Antalya-style tahini piyaz since 1996, the white-bean salad that locals eat as a main course. The menu also has grilled and şiş köfte, soups and pumpkin dessert.
new.tip: Open daily from about 11:30 to 21:30; come at lunch for the shortest wait.
new.q: Piyazcı Ahmet, 166. Sokak 29/A, Altındağ, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Treat yourself at Salman Pastanesi
new.desc: A long-standing patisserie recommended in easyJet's Antalya food guide.
new.tip: Try the local pastries.

new.title: Cool down with Akdeniz Dondurma
new.desc: A local ice-cream shop recommended by Culture Trip among Antalya's foods to try.
new.tip: Try the stretchy Maraş-style ice cream.

new.title: Eat piyaz at Meşhur Aksu Şimşek Köfteci İsa
new.desc: A köfte and piyaz restaurant in Aksu district with live music, a locals' pick.
new.tip: Go with a group for the music.
new.q: Aksu Şimşek Köfte Piyaz, Aksu, Antalya

new.title: Have Turkish breakfast at Varuna Gezgin Cafe
new.desc: A Kaleiçi café known for its breakfast menu.
new.tip: Expect higher prices than outside the old town.
new.q: Varuna Gezgin Cafe, Hamam Sokak 2/1, Kılınçarslan, Kaleiçi, Muratpaşa, Antalya
